newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil allows exporters to raise capital overseas.
newsitem.headline: Brazil allows exporters to raise capital overseas.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank Thursday announced new rules allowing banks to raise capital overseas to lend to exporters, a spokesman said.

Financial institutions will be able to place bonds abroad and use the resources to lend capital to Brazilian exporters with 180-day maturities, well below the three-year average maturities of overseas issues.
The interest rate charged will be set by the Central Bank and the capital inflows will be exempt from IOF financial transaction taxes, the spokesman said.
The spokesman said the bank calculated that overseas issues would pay some 9.0 percent a year interest and that the domestic rate for exporters would be between 11 percent and 13 percent.
Raising capital overseas for exports had been limited to agricultural goods.
The Brazilian government has recently vowed to boost exports by, among other measures, exempting shipments from export taxes.
Brazil so far this year is running a trade deficit in the region of $630 million, compared with a $3.157 billion deficit in the whole of 1995 and a $10 billion surplus the year before.
